NoteTexAccessor::pm_signs¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteTexAccessor::pm_signs() const

Render Paired-Sign Control Words As Plain Text¶

pm_signs() converts the complete TeX control word \pm to +/- and \mp to -/+. The ordering is intentional: \pm means plus over minus, while \mp carries the complementary minus-over-plus order commonly used in a paired expression.

Matching follows TeX control-word boundaries. \pmatrix is one different control word, not \pm followed by atrix, and therefore remains untouched. The scanner also distinguishes the linebreak control symbol \\; letters following that symbol are not consumed as a command. This is materially safer than raw substring replacement in documents containing matrix-like macro names or escaped source fragments.

The operation replaces syntax only. It does not choose one branch of an equation, duplicate an expression into two alternatives, alter surrounding spacing, or remove math delimiters. Comments are ordinary source text at this stage, so call strip_comments() first if commented commands should be ignored.

The result is a new shape-preserving Text Note. Unmatched cells are copied, empty cells remain empty, and undefined input remains undefined. Native non-Text dtypes reject. Each lane is scanned once, and output allocation is proportional to the resulting byte count; the receiver is unchanged.

Example 1: Both Sign Orders¶

const auto signs = pluss::make_note({R"(x \pm e)", R"(y \mp d)"});
std::cout << signs.tex().pm_signs() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["x +/- e", "y -/+ d"]

Example 2: Command And Control-Symbol Boundaries¶

const auto boundaries = pluss::make_note(
    {R"(x \pm e, y \mp d)", R"(\pmatrix and \\pm stay TeX)"});
std::cout << boundaries.tex().pm_signs() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["x +/- e, y -/+ d", "\\pmatrix and \\\\pm stay TeX"]

Example 3: Shape Preservation And Unmatched Cells¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(a\pm b)", "plain", R"(c\mp d)", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().pm_signs() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a+/- b", "plain"], 
  ["c-/+ d", ""]
]

Example 4: Undefined Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().pm_signs().defined()
          << '\n';

Output¶

false

Example 5: Non-Text Input Rejects¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().pm_signs();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "plus-minus Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

plus-minus Int64: rejected
